correctness.rationale: Equilibrium existence and global attraction follow from explicit logistic comparison and a strict max-ratio uniqueness argument. Ellipsoid sum identity, unique optimizer, and exact squared-distance deficit follow algebraically. Max-flow/min-cut gives the exact necessary and sufficient no-outgoing-subset condition for finite nonnegative directed downhill flux, translated to finite symmetric conductances by positive target-density differences. Rational feasible witness verifies every ODE equation; rational obstruction yields a strict violated cut; independently coded exact-fraction flow/cut tests complement the proof, not replace it.

originality.rationale: 2020 primary source already proves the biomass ceiling and the unique ellipsoid optimizer; this is explicitly credited. Novelty is restricted to the theorem identifying exactly when finite NONNEGATIVE SYMMETRIC conductances on a prescribed topology realize that known optimizer, via directed intrinsic-growth cut constraints, and to its constructive proof. Full original paper and supplementary statement comparisons show distinct assumptions and quantifiers; multi-patch symmetric and two-patch finite literature do not dominate the new arbitrary-graph finite realization criterion. Actual research-index semantic checks found no equivalent statement; this is a literature-qualified assessment, not an exhaustive uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: General inverse graph Laplacian and network design literature outside the inspected ecological sources may contain an algebraically equivalent theorem.
Published abstract/index retrieval is incomplete, so scientific originality is provisional to wider independent literature search.
Unbounded selectable finite edge coefficients are essential; prescribed edge budgets or strictly positive-on-all-edge requirements are different problems.

value.rationale: The known upper bound by itself does not answer whether a fixed ecological corridor network can realize the theoretical maximum at any finite symmetric movement rates. The theorem supplies a sharp topology-sensitive feasibility criterion and constructive design, including arbitrary tied target densities and disconnected landscapes. Feasible and impossible three-patch witnesses show real nontrivial separation between mathematical ceiling and engineering attainability; this is a natural ecological design question rather than a routine numeric slice.
